countries.name: France
countries.blurb: A country that changes character every few hours of driving — Atlantic cliffs, Alpine passes, Mediterranean heat, and a capital that rewards wandering.
countries.uniqueness: France packs a dozen distinct climates and cuisines into one country, connected by fast trains. The south runs warm and dry, the north cool and grey, and the Alps keep their own calendar — which means the right month depends entirely on which France you're going to.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: 15–22°C, gardens open, museums quiet. Lavender isn't out yet, but the Loire and Dordogne are at their greenest and prices haven't peaked.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Often above 30°C in the south. Lavender blooms in Valensole through June and July, coastal towns are full, and prices peak. Paris empties of Parisians in August.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: Widely considered the sweet spot — warm sea, wine harvest under way, calmer streets. September in particular balances weather against crowds.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Cheapest flights and rooms. Alsace Christmas markets run through December, the Alps open for snow, and city museums are at their least crowded.

activities.title: Walk the Louvre before the tour groups arrive
activities.description: The world's most-visited museum is a different place in its first hour. Entry is timed, and the least-crowded rooms are often the ones furthest from the Mona Lisa.

activities.title: Watch the light change at Sainte-Chapelle
activities.description: Fifteen metres of 13th-century stained glass wrapping a single upper chapel. Sunny late mornings put the most colour on the stone.

activities.title: Stand on the D-Day beaches in Normandy
activities.description: Omaha, Utah, Juno and the cliffs at Pointe du Hoc, with the American cemetery above. Long, quiet, wind-blown stretches of coast that carry their history plainly.

activities.title: Cross to Mont-Saint-Michel at high tide
activities.description: A medieval abbey stacked on a tidal island off the Normandy coast. Tide tables decide whether it stands on sand or in water — the difference is dramatic.

activities.title: See the cave paintings near the Dordogne
activities.description: Some of the oldest known art in Europe sits under the limestone of the Vézère valley. Original caves are strictly limited; several are shown through exact replicas.

activities.title: Château-hop through the Loire Valley
activities.description: Over 300 châteaux across one valley — Chambord for scale, Chenonceau for its arches over the river, Villandry for the gardens.

activities.title: Follow the wine harvest in Burgundy or Bordeaux
activities.description: Late summer into autumn, whole villages turn to picking. Many estates open their doors, and the roads smell of fermenting fruit.

activities.title: Eat your way through a Provençal market morning
activities.description: Cheeses, honey, olives, herbs and knife-sharpeners under plane trees. Most markets run one or two mornings a week and are packed up by lunch.

activities.title: Sit down to a long lunch in Lyon
activities.description: The bouchons of Lyon serve the unfussy end of French cooking — quenelles, andouillette, pralines — in rooms that haven't changed much in decades.

activities.title: Taste Champagne where it's made
activities.description: The chalk cellars under Reims and Épernay run for kilometres. Houses range from grand names to small growers who'll sit and talk.

activities.title: Stand in the lavender at Valensole
activities.description: The Provence plateau turns purple in early summer. Bloom timing shifts each year with the weather, and fields are working farms, not parks.

activities.title: Drive the Verdon Gorge
activities.description: Limestone walls above turquoise water, with pull-offs the whole way round. Kayaks and pedalos launch from the lake at the western end.

activities.title: Ride the cable car under Mont Blanc
activities.description: The Aiguille du Midi lift climbs to 3,842m for a face-on view of the massif. Weather closes it often; clear mornings are the reliable window.

activities.title: Walk a stage of the Tour du Mont Blanc
activities.description: The full circuit takes ten days across three countries, but single stages from Chamonix give you the high passes without the commitment.

activities.title: Ski or hike the Alps out of Chamonix or Annecy
activities.description: Winter brings some of Europe's longest verticals; summer turns the same slopes into trails and paragliding launches above Lake Annecy.

activities.title: Cycle the vineyard lanes of Alsace
activities.description: Flat, well-signed routes link half-timbered villages between Strasbourg and Colmar, with tasting rooms roughly every few kilometres.

activities.title: Swim the calanques near Marseille
activities.description: White limestone inlets dropping into clear water, reachable on foot, by kayak or by boat. Summer fire risk closes some trails at short notice.

activities.title: Take the coast road along the Côte d'Azur
activities.description: The corniches between Nice and Menton stack three roads at three heights, each with a different view of the same sea.

activities.title: Ride Paris by night on the river
activities.description: The Seine boats run late, and the city's monuments are lit until around 1am. It's the cheapest way to see the whole centre in an hour.

activities.title: Wander Strasbourg's Christmas markets
activities.description: One of Europe's oldest, running through Advent across several squares, with Alsace's food and mulled wine and a lot of cold air.

activities.title: Do nothing in a village square
activities.description: A coffee, a newspaper you can't read, and an hour watching a place go about its day — arguably the most French thing on this list.

countries.name: Japan
countries.blurb: Dense, quiet, precise, and far stranger than the postcards — a country where a bullet train drops you at a thousand-year-old pilgrimage trail.
countries.uniqueness: Japan runs on seasons more than most places: what's worth seeing shifts week by week, tracked nationally. Blossom moves north for a month; autumn colour moves south for two. And volcanic geology means over 2,000 natural hot springs, most of them in small towns rather than resorts.

seasons.label: Cherry blossom
seasons.note: Tokyo and Kyoto peak roughly 28 March–3 April, later further north. Spectacular, but the busiest and most expensive weeks of the year.

seasons.label: Late spring
seasons.note: Widely rated the best all-round month — mild, dry, green, and far calmer than blossom season.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Hot and humid with a rainy spell in June; festival season, and the only window for climbing Fuji. Hokkaido stays comfortable.

seasons.label: Autumn colour
seasons.note: Koyo starts in Hokkaido in September and reaches Kyoto and Tokyo from mid-October into November. Second-busiest season, and worth it.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Powder snow in the north, quiet temples in Kyoto, and the best time for onsen — steam and snow together.

activities.title: Walk a stage of the Kumano Kodo
activities.description: Pilgrimage trails through the Kii Peninsula walked for over a thousand years, linking mountain shrines. The Nakahechi route is the classic; the Iseji sees a fraction of the traffic.

activities.title: Soak in a riverside onsen at Kawayu
activities.description: Hot water rises through the riverbed itself. In winter the river is dammed to make a single enormous open-air bath.

activities.title: Bathe your way around Kinosaki
activities.description: A hot-spring town of seven public bathhouses, walked between in a yukata and wooden sandals under willow-lined canals.

activities.title: See the steam vents at Beppu
activities.description: More than 2,000 hot springs in one town, including the 'hells' — thermal pools too hot to enter, plus mud and sand baths that you can.

activities.title: Take the waters at Kusatsu
activities.description: High in the Gunma mountains, with enormous volumes of hot water cooled by hand in wooden channels in a display locals have done for generations.

activities.title: Stay a night in a ryokan
activities.description: Tatami floors, futons laid out while you're at dinner, and a multi-course kaiseki meal built around what's in season locally.

activities.title: Watch morning prayers at Sensō-ji
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, in Asakusa. Early morning belongs to people who actually pray there, before the approach fills with stalls and crowds.

activities.title: Walk the forest path to Meiji Shrine
activities.description: A hundred thousand donated trees planted around a shrine in central Tokyo. Weekend mornings often bring traditional wedding processions.

activities.title: Take the temple circuit in Kyoto
activities.description: Kiyomizu-dera's terrace, the vermilion tunnels at Fushimi Inari, the moss and raked gravel of the Zen gardens. Early or late avoids the worst of it.

activities.title: See Nara's deer among the temples
activities.description: Sika deer roam freely around Tōdai-ji and its enormous bronze Buddha, an hour from Kyoto or Osaka.

activities.title: Sit under the blossom at a hanami party
activities.description: Parks fill with tarps, food and quiet celebration for the two weeks the trees hold. Some shrines light the trees after dark.

activities.title: Chase the autumn colour south
activities.description: Koyo works down the country over two months — Hokkaido first, Kyoto's maples last. Temple gardens are built around the display.

activities.title: Cross the island of Naoshima by bike
activities.description: A small Seto Inland Sea island turned over to contemporary art — Tadao Ando concrete museums, a Kusama pumpkin on the pier, and old houses rebuilt as installations.

activities.title: Stand at Shibuya Crossing at rush hour
activities.description: Several thousand people crossing at once, several times an hour. The upper floors of the surrounding buildings are where you actually see the pattern.

activities.title: Eat standing up at a market counter
activities.description: Tsukiji's outer market and Kyoto's Nishiki are lined with single-dish stalls — grilled scallops, tamagoyaki, tuna cut in front of you.

activities.title: Find a six-seat izakaya
activities.description: The small alleys — Omoide Yokocho, Golden Gai, Pontocho — hide bars with room for a handful of people and a menu on the wall.

activities.title: Take a soba or sushi class
activities.description: Hands-on sessions run in most cities, usually a couple of hours, usually ending with eating what you made.

activities.title: Ride the shinkansen with Fuji on the right
activities.description: Tokyo to Kyoto in a bit over two hours. Sit on the right leaving Tokyo and watch for Fuji roughly 40 minutes in, on clear days.

activities.title: Climb Mount Fuji overnight
activities.description: The official season is short and the mountain is busy within it. Most climb through the night from a mid-mountain station to reach the crater for sunrise.

activities.title: Ski the powder in Hokkaido or Nagano
activities.description: Some of the most consistent snowfall anywhere, with onsen at the bottom of the runs and monkeys bathing in them near Nagano.

activities.title: Ferry through the Seto Inland Sea
activities.description: Slow boats between small islands, olive groves and art sites, on a stretch of water dotted with several hundred islands.

countries.name: Italy
countries.blurb: Twenty regions that barely agree on anything — least of all food — stacked with more ruins, frescoes and coastline than any itinerary can hold.
countries.uniqueness: Italy was a collection of separate states until 1861, and it still behaves like one. Dialect, bread, cheese and pasta shape change every hour or two of driving, which is why 'Italian food' means almost nothing once you're actually there.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Wildflowers, green hills, warm days without the heat. Easter is the exception — busy and priced accordingly.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Hot, crowded and expensive, especially the coast. Cities empty of locals in mid-August as Italians take their own holidays.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: The sweet spot: the sea is still warm enough to swim into October, harvest and truffle season begin, and prices drop 25–35% from the August peak.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Museums and cities without queues, ski season in the Dolomites, Venice at its quietest and moodiest. Many coastal towns close entirely.

activities.title: Walk the Roman Forum at opening time
activities.description: The centre of an empire, now roofless and grass-grown, with the Colosseum at one end. Early entry avoids both the heat and the tour flags.

activities.title: Stand in front of the Sistine Chapel ceiling
activities.description: Four years of Michelangelo's work, viewed with your neck bent, in a room where guards ask for silence. The Vatican Museums leading to it are a marathon in themselves.

activities.title: Walk into a city stopped mid-morning at Pompeii
activities.description: Streets, bakeries, graffiti and plaster casts of the people who didn't leave, under Vesuvius. Herculaneum nearby is smaller, better preserved and far quieter.
activities.when: Spring and autumn — no shade in summer

activities.title: See the Renaissance where it started, in Florence
activities.description: The Uffizi, the Accademia's David, Brunelleschi's dome you can still climb. Concentrated enough to see on foot in two days.

activities.title: Take the vaporetto to Venice's outer islands
activities.description: Burano's painted houses, Murano's glass furnaces, Torcello's near-empty cathedral. The lagoon starts making sense once you leave San Marco.

activities.title: Eat where the dish was invented
activities.description: Carbonara in Rome, ragù in Bologna, pizza in Naples, pesto in Genoa. The versions differ enough from the exports to be worth the trip.

activities.title: Spend a morning in Bologna's Quadrilatero
activities.description: The old market lanes behind the main square — mortadella, tortellini rolled in windows, cheese wheels the size of tables.

activities.title: Hunt truffles in Piedmont or Umbria
activities.description: Autumn brings white truffle season around Alba, with dogs doing the finding and markets doing the arguing over price.

activities.title: Drink Barolo where the grapes grow
activities.description: The Langhe hills south of Turin — small cellars, long lunches, and views over vineyards that turn gold in October.

activities.title: Hike between the Cinque Terre villages
activities.description: Five cliffside towns linked by coastal paths above the Ligurian Sea. Some sections require a pass, and landslides close others without warning.

activities.title: Walk under the Dolomites
activities.description: Vertical limestone towers with well-marked trails and mountain huts serving dumplings. The rock turns pink at sunset — locals call it enrosadira.

activities.title: Climb an active volcano
activities.description: Etna in Sicily can be walked or reached by cable car and jeep; Stromboli erupts most nights and can be watched from a boat offshore.

activities.title: Drive the Amalfi Coast
activities.description: A cliff road of blind corners, lemon terraces and towns stacked above the sea. Buses and ferries save you the parking problem entirely.

activities.title: Swim off Sardinia or Puglia
activities.description: Sardinia's water is famously clear; Puglia's coast is flatter, cheaper and dotted with whitewashed towns and sea caves.

activities.title: Take a boat into the Blue Grotto or around Capri
activities.description: Sea caves lit from below through the water. Access depends entirely on swell, so it's a morning decision, not a booking.

activities.title: Wander Matera's cave dwellings
activities.description: A town of houses carved into a ravine, abandoned as a slum and now partly restored. Lit at night it looks like a nativity scene.

activities.title: See Milan for design rather than sightseeing
activities.description: Furniture showrooms, Navigli canals, aperitivo hour, and the Last Supper if you booked months ago.

activities.title: Sit through an opera in Verona's Roman arena
activities.description: A 2,000-year-old amphitheatre used for summer opera, where the audience lights candles as the sun goes down.

activities.title: Ride the slow trains through Tuscany
activities.description: Regional lines link Siena, San Gimignano and the Val d'Orcia's cypress ridges without the stress of hill-town parking.

activities.title: Take the passeggiata seriously
activities.description: The evening walk before dinner, done by whole towns at once, dressed properly. It costs nothing and explains a lot about Italy.

activities.title: Soak in a thermal bath in Tuscany
activities.description: Saturnia's terraced hot pools are free and open all hours; Bagno Vignoni has a whole medieval square filled with steaming water.

countries.name: Spain
countries.blurb: Late dinners, Moorish palaces, Atlantic surf and Mediterranean heat — a country that runs on a clock several hours behind the rest of Europe.
countries.uniqueness: Eight centuries of Moorish rule left architecture, irrigation and words you'll still hear daily, and several regions speak their own language entirely. Add a national schedule where dinner starts at 10pm and nothing about Spain fits a generic European template.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Green countryside, wildflowers, comfortable cities. Seville's Feria and Easter processions fall here and fill the south.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Inland Andalusia regularly passes 40°C; the north coast stays mild and green. August sees much of the country on holiday at once.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: Sea still warm, cities workable again, prices well below the August peak. Grape harvest across Rioja and Ribera.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Mild in the south, cold and clear in Madrid, snow in the Pyrenees and Sierra Nevada. The Canaries stay swimmable throughout.

activities.title: Walk through the Alhambra
activities.description: A Moorish palace-fortress above Granada with carved stucco, still courtyards and water used as architecture. Ticket numbers are capped daily and sell out weeks ahead.

activities.title: Stand inside the Mezquita of Córdoba
activities.description: A forest of red-and-white arches from a 10th-century mosque, with a cathedral dropped into the middle of it in the 16th.

activities.title: Watch Gaudí's Sagrada Família catch the light
activities.description: Still unfinished after 140 years. Morning light comes through blue and green glass, afternoon through orange and red.

activities.title: See the Prado's Velázquez and Goya rooms
activities.description: Las Meninas and the Black Paintings in one building. Free entry in the last two hours of the day, if you don't mind company.

activities.title: Walk a stretch of the Camino de Santiago
activities.description: Pilgrim routes crossing northern Spain, walked for over a thousand years. Many people do the last 100km from Sarria, which qualifies for the certificate.

activities.title: Eat pintxos bar to bar in San Sebastián
activities.description: Basque bar snacks pinned to bread, taken standing, one or two per bar before moving on. The old town is built for exactly this.

activities.title: Have paella where it comes from
activities.description: Valencia's version uses rabbit, chicken and beans — not seafood — and is cooked over wood for lunch, never dinner.

activities.title: Drink sherry in Jerez
activities.description: Cellars of stacked barrels where the wine is blended across decades. Bone dry, served cold, and nothing like the sweet stuff exported for years.

activities.title: Follow the harvest through Rioja
activities.description: Villages between Logroño and Haro fill with pickers in autumn, and cellars range from centuries-old to Frank Gehry.

activities.title: Sit close at a small flamenco show
activities.description: A tablao with a few dozen seats, where you hear the breathing and the floor. Andalusia — Seville, Jerez, Granada — is where it lives.

activities.title: Hike the Picos de Europa
activities.description: Limestone peaks an hour from the north coast, with cable cars, gorge walks and cheese caves. Greener and wetter than most people expect of Spain.

activities.title: Walk the Caminito del Rey
activities.description: A walkway bolted to a gorge wall a hundred metres above the river, rebuilt after decades as one of the world's most dangerous paths.

activities.title: Surf or storm-watch the Atlantic north
activities.description: Cantabria and the Basque coast get proper swell, green hills behind and seafood towns along the shore.

activities.title: Island-hop the Balearics
activities.description: Mallorca's mountains and coves, Menorca's quiet beaches, Ibiza's other side once you leave the clubs. Ferries link all three.

activities.title: Swim in the Canaries in winter
activities.description: Volcanic islands off Africa where the sea stays swimmable in January. Lanzarote's lava fields look like nowhere else in Europe.

activities.title: Sleep in a parador
activities.description: State-run hotels inside castles, monasteries and convents. Often the most interesting building in town, at a normal hotel price.

activities.title: Take a siesta seriously in summer
activities.description: Shops shut, streets empty, and the country reappears at seven. Fighting it in 40°C heat is a losing battle.

activities.title: See a city taken over by a festival
activities.description: Las Fallas burns giant sculptures in Valencia each March; Pamplona runs bulls in July; Buñol throws tomatoes in August.

activities.title: Wander the white villages of Andalusia
activities.description: Ronda's gorge bridge, Setenil built under a rock overhang, and dozens of others strung across the hills between Málaga and Cádiz.

activities.title: See Bilbao's Guggenheim and what it did to the city
activities.description: Gehry's titanium curves turned a declining industrial port into an art destination — the most cited example of a building changing a city's fortunes.

activities.title: Watch the sun set over Cádiz
activities.description: The oldest continuously inhabited city in western Europe, on a spit of land with the Atlantic on three sides.

countries.name: Greece
countries.blurb: Six thousand islands, a few hundred inhabited, wrapped around a mainland of mountains, monasteries and ruins that shaped most of what came after.
countries.uniqueness: The scale of the island count changes how you travel — ferries are the road network, and choosing between Cyclades, Ionian and Dodecanese means choosing between genuinely different landscapes, food and architecture.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Wildflowers, green hills, warm days and cold sea. Ruins without queues and islands before the ferries get busy.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Hot, dry and full. The meltemi wind cools the Cyclades and cancels the odd ferry. August is the peak of everything, including prices.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: The warmest sea of the year, thinning crowds and softer light. Many consider it the best month-and-a-half in Greece.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Athens stays mild and museum-friendly, mountain villages get snow, and most small islands close down almost entirely.

activities.title: Climb to the Acropolis early
activities.description: The Parthenon above Athens, best in the first hour when the marble is cool and the light is still low.

activities.title: See what came off the Acropolis, in the museum below
activities.description: The Acropolis Museum's top floor is built to the temple's exact proportions, with glass walls facing the real thing.

activities.title: Stand where the oracle spoke at Delphi
activities.description: A sanctuary on the slope of Mount Parnassus that the Greeks considered the centre of the world, with the valley falling away below.

activities.title: Walk the ruins of Knossos on Crete
activities.description: A Bronze Age palace complex, partly reconstructed in concrete by its excavator — controversial, but it makes the scale readable.

activities.title: Climb to the monasteries at Meteora
activities.description: Monasteries built on sandstone pillars, reached by steps cut into rock. Still working communities, with dress codes to match.

activities.title: Watch the sun go down over the Santorini caldera
activities.description: The rim of a collapsed volcano, whitewashed villages along the edge. Crowded and worth it; Imerovigli is quieter than Oia.

activities.title: Ferry-hop the Cyclades
activities.description: Paros, Naxos, Milos, Folegandros — an hour or two apart, each with different beaches, food and levels of noise.

activities.title: Swim at Milos's volcanic coves
activities.description: Sarakiniko's white rock looks lunar; other beaches on the same island are red, black or reachable only by boat.

activities.title: Sail the Ionian islands
activities.description: Greener and wetter than the Cyclades, with calmer water. Corfu, Kefalonia and Lefkada are all in easy hopping range.

activities.title: Walk the Samaria Gorge
activities.description: Sixteen kilometres down through a Cretan gorge to the sea, ending where the only way out is by boat.

activities.title: Hike the stone paths of the Zagori villages
activities.description: Arched bridges, slate roofs and the Vikos Gorge in the mountains of Epirus — a completely different Greece from the islands.

activities.title: Eat in a taverna where there's no menu
activities.description: You're shown the pots, you point. Common in villages, and usually the best meal of the trip.

activities.title: Take mezze seriously with ouzo
activities.description: Small plates arriving slowly over hours, meant to be shared while the anise clouds in the glass. Lesvos is the ouzo heartland.

activities.title: Visit an olive mill at pressing time
activities.description: Late autumn brings the harvest, when the first oil is green, cloudy and peppery enough to catch in the throat.

activities.title: Eat Cretan food in the hills
activities.description: Wild greens, snails, barley rusks and cheese from small producers — a diet studied for decades for its longevity.

activities.title: Watch the old town of Rhodes at night
activities.description: A medieval walled city built by the Knights of St John, still lived in, with cobbles worn smooth.

activities.title: Wander Nafplio's marble streets
activities.description: Greece's first capital after independence — Venetian fortresses, bougainvillea and a harbour, three hours from Athens.

activities.title: Take the rack railway up the Vouraikos Gorge
activities.description: A narrow-gauge line clinging to a gorge wall in the Peloponnese, running between Diakopto and Kalavryta.

activities.title: Spend a day doing nothing on a small island
activities.description: One beach, one bakery, one ferry a day. Islands like Koufonisia and Sikinos are built for exactly this.

activities.title: Join a village festival
activities.description: Saints' days bring whole villages out for food, wine and dancing that runs past midnight, especially through August.

activities.title: See the Corinth Canal cut
activities.description: A 6km channel sliced through solid rock, 80m deep and barely 20m wide — best seen from the bridge above.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.blurb: Atlantic light, tiled facades, cork forests and a coastline that goes from surf breaks to still lagoons in a few hours' drive.
countries.uniqueness: Portugal faces the Atlantic rather than the Mediterranean, which changes everything — the water is colder, the waves are bigger, the light is sharper, and the food leans on salt cod and grilled sardines rather than olive oil and tomato.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Wildflowers in the Alentejo, comfortable cities, cold ocean. Prices and crowds well below summer.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Lisbon averages around 28°C and Porto 26°C — the Atlantic keeps it milder than inland Spain. Many local restaurants close for holidays in August.

seasons.label: Early autumn
seasons.note: The warmest sea of the year, grape harvest in the Douro, and 25–35% off August prices.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Mild and rainy in the north, gentler in the Algarve. Nazaré's giant waves arrive, and Madeira stays green and walkable.

activities.title: Ride tram 28 through Lisbon's hills
activities.description: A wooden streetcar grinding up through Alfama and Graça. Board at the start of the line if you want a seat rather than a wrestle.

activities.title: Listen to fado in a small room
activities.description: Sung mourning, roughly — one voice and a Portuguese guitar, in Alfama or Mouraria, usually late and usually with dinner.

activities.title: Walk the palaces of Sintra
activities.description: Pena's painted turrets, Quinta da Regaleira's initiation well spiralling underground, all in mist half the year. Forty minutes from Lisbon by train.

activities.title: Taste port in Vila Nova de Gaia
activities.description: Cross the river from Porto to the lodges where port ages. Tawny and ruby taste nothing alike, and the tour explains why.

activities.title: Take the train up the Douro Valley
activities.description: The line hugs the river past terraced vineyards cut into slate hillsides — one of Europe's best rail rides, and cheap.

activities.title: Watch the giant waves at Nazaré
activities.description: An underwater canyon focuses swell into waves that have topped 20 metres. Watched from the lighthouse headland when the forecast lines up.

activities.title: Learn to surf on the Atlantic coast
activities.description: Peniche, Ericeira and Costa da Caparica have beginner beaches and schools by the dozen, with consistent year-round swell.

activities.title: Kayak the sea caves of the Algarve
activities.description: Golden limestone arches and hidden beaches around Benagil, reachable only from the water.

activities.title: Walk the cliffs of the Rota Vicentina
activities.description: A coastal path down the southwest, along cliffs and empty beaches where storks nest on sea stacks.

activities.title: Eat grilled sardines in summer
activities.description: Charcoal, salt, bread underneath to catch the oil. June brings street festivals in Lisbon built around exactly this.

activities.title: Work out what to do with bacalhau
activities.description: Salt cod, said to have a recipe for every day of the year. Brás and à Gomes de Sá are the ones worth starting with.

activities.title: Queue for a pastel de nata
activities.description: Custard tart, burnt on top, best warm with cinnamon. Belém's original bakery has been making them since 1837.

activities.title: See azulejo tilework up close
activities.description: Blue-and-white tiles cover churches, stations and whole facades. Porto's São Bento station and Lisbon's tile museum are the concentrated versions.

activities.title: Walk in Madeira's levada channels
activities.description: Irrigation channels cut across the island's cliffs centuries ago, with footpaths beside them running through laurel forest.

activities.title: Cross to the Azores
activities.description: Volcanic islands mid-Atlantic — crater lakes, hot springs, hydrangea hedges, and some of the best whale watching in Europe.

activities.title: Drive through the cork oaks of the Alentejo
activities.description: Rolling plains, stripped cork trunks, whitewashed villages and almost no traffic. Portugal produces about half the world's cork.

activities.title: Stay inside a monastery or castle
activities.description: The pousada network puts hotels in historic buildings — Óbidos inside the castle walls, Évora in a convent.

activities.title: See the bone chapel in Évora
activities.description: Walls lined with the bones of some 5,000 monks, built as a meditation on mortality, with an inscription at the door to match.

activities.title: Stand at Cabo da Roca
activities.description: The westernmost point of mainland Europe — a cliff, a lighthouse, and a lot of wind.

activities.title: Sit at a miradouro at golden hour
activities.description: Lisbon's viewpoints are institutions, usually with a kiosk selling beer and someone playing guitar badly.

activities.title: Wander Porto's Ribeira after dark
activities.description: The riverfront under the Dom Luís bridge, lit and busy, with port lodges glowing on the far bank.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.blurb: Street food that outclasses restaurants, temples in every direction, and two coastlines whose weather works in opposite directions.
countries.uniqueness: Thailand's two coasts run on opposite monsoon cycles — when the Andaman side is being rained on, the Gulf side is often sunny, and vice versa. It's one of the few countries where picking the right beach is mostly a question of which month it is.

seasons.label: Cool and dry
seasons.note: The best all-round window nationwide — comfortable heat, low rain, and both coasts generally workable. Also the busiest and priciest.

seasons.label: Hot season
seasons.note: Genuinely hot, into the high 30s. Songkran in mid-April turns the whole country into a water fight for several days.

seasons.label: Green season
seasons.note: Rain in short heavy bursts rather than all day, landscapes at their greenest and prices at their lowest. September–October are the wettest.

seasons.label: Coast timing
seasons.note: Andaman side (Phuket, Krabi, Koh Lanta) is best November–April. Gulf side (Samui, Phangan, Tao) is better January–August, with heaviest rain October–November.

activities.title: Eat dinner from a plastic stool
activities.description: Bangkok's street food runs from noodle carts to Michelin-listed stalls. The queue of locals is the only review that matters.

activities.title: Take a boat through Bangkok's canals
activities.description: The city was built on water before it was built on roads. Longtail boats still run the khlongs behind the main river.

activities.title: See the Grand Palace and Wat Pho
activities.description: Gold, mirror mosaic and a 46-metre reclining Buddha. Strict dress code — covered shoulders and knees, enforced at the gate.

activities.title: Watch monks collect alms at dawn
activities.description: A daily ritual in most towns, at its most striking in Luang-style processions through Chiang Mai's old city before sunrise.

activities.title: Cycle the ruins of Ayutthaya
activities.description: A former capital sacked in 1767, its brick temples and a Buddha head grown into tree roots, an hour north of Bangkok.

activities.title: Walk among Sukhothai's lotus ponds
activities.description: The first Thai kingdom's capital, quieter and greener than Ayutthaya, best on a bicycle in early light.

activities.title: Take a cooking class in Chiang Mai
activities.description: Usually starts at a market picking herbs, ends with you eating four dishes you made and a recipe book you'll actually use.

activities.title: Spend a morning at a fresh market
activities.description: Chiang Mai's Warorot, Bangkok's Or Tor Kor — fruit you won't recognise, curry pastes ground on the spot, and breakfast.

activities.title: Visit an ethical elephant sanctuary
activities.description: Places where elephants are observed rather than ridden or bathed on demand. Riding and forced bathing remain widespread — the distinction is worth researching before booking.

activities.title: Watch the lanterns rise at Yi Peng
activities.description: Thousands of paper lanterns released in Chiang Mai in November, alongside Loy Krathong's floating candles on the water.

activities.title: Get soaked at Songkran
activities.description: Thai new year, marked with three days of nationwide water fights. Nothing stays dry, including you and your phone.

activities.title: Kayak the limestone karsts of Phang Nga Bay
activities.description: Vertical islands, sea caves and hidden lagoons reached by paddling under low rock at the right tide.

activities.title: Dive or snorkel off Koh Tao
activities.description: One of the cheapest places in the world to get certified, with shallow reefs and whale sharks passing through.

activities.title: Find a quieter island
activities.description: Koh Lanta, Koh Kood and Koh Yao Noi trade nightlife for hammocks, and are usually a ferry further than most people go.
activities.when: Depends on coast — see When to go

activities.title: Ride the Mae Hong Son loop
activities.description: Around 600km of mountain switchbacks in the north, through hill villages, hot springs and coffee-growing valleys.

activities.title: Trek into Khao Sok's rainforest
activities.description: Older than the Amazon, with limestone cliffs above a reservoir and floating bungalows you wake up in surrounded by water.

activities.title: Sit through a Muay Thai night
activities.description: Live bouts at Bangkok's Rajadamnern or Lumpinee stadiums, with the crowd's betting more theatrical than the fight.

activities.title: Get a proper Thai massage
activities.description: Stretching and pressure rather than oil and relaxation — Wat Pho runs the school that trained most of the country.

activities.title: Take the night train south
activities.description: Sleeper berths from Bangkok toward Surat Thani, with curtains, cold air and a morning arrival for the Gulf ferries.

activities.title: Wander a floating market at opening
activities.description: Damnoen Saduak and Amphawa are both busy by mid-morning; the first hour is when they're still functioning as markets.

activities.title: Do nothing on a beach in the green season
activities.description: Rain comes in bursts, the crowds thin out, and a beach hut costs a fraction of the December rate.

countries.name: United States of America
countries.blurb: A continent pretending to be a country — deserts, glaciers, swamps, canyons and cities that share a currency and not much else.
countries.uniqueness: The distances are the thing people underestimate. Los Angeles to New York is further than London to Cairo, and the national parks system protects landscapes on a scale — canyons a mile deep, trees older than most nations — that doesn't really exist elsewhere.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: Desert blooms in the southwest, cherry blossom in Washington, and the shoulder window before park crowds arrive.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Peak season for the parks and Alaska, and the only reliable window for high-altitude trails. Southern deserts hit dangerous heat.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: New England's leaves turn, national parks quieten, and the southwest becomes comfortable again. Widely the best all-round month-and-a-half.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Ski season in the Rockies, Florida and southern California at their best, and northern parks either closed or transformed.

activities.title: Stand on the rim of the Grand Canyon at sunrise
activities.description: A mile deep and up to eighteen wide. The South Rim is open year-round; the North Rim closes for winter and sees a fraction of the visitors.

activities.title: Watch geysers and bison in Yellowstone
activities.description: The world's first national park, sitting on an active supervolcano — hot springs, mud pots, wolves and traffic jams caused by bison.

activities.title: Look up at Yosemite's granite walls
activities.description: El Capitan and Half Dome above a valley floor, with waterfalls that run hardest in late spring and often dry by August.

activities.title: Walk among the world's largest trees
activities.description: Sequoia and Redwood parks in California — trees wide enough to drive through and older than the Roman Empire.

activities.title: Drive through Utah's canyon country
activities.description: Zion, Bryce, Arches and Canyonlands sit within a few hours of each other — red rock, hoodoos and arches, all in one loop.

activities.title: Cross Death Valley in the cool months
activities.description: The lowest, driest and hottest place in North America. Summer temperatures pass 50°C and are genuinely dangerous.

activities.title: Take the ferry past the Statue of Liberty
activities.description: The Staten Island ferry is free and passes close enough. Ellis Island next door is where 12 million arrivals were processed.

activities.title: Hear live music in New Orleans
activities.description: Brass on Frenchmen Street rather than Bourbon, second-line parades on Sundays, and jazz in rooms the size of living rooms.

activities.title: Eat your way through a city's immigrant neighbourhoods
activities.description: Queens in New York, Houston's Asiatown, LA's San Gabriel Valley — arguably the most interesting food in the country.

activities.title: Follow the barbecue belt
activities.description: Texas brisket, Carolina whole hog, Memphis ribs, Kansas City burnt ends — four regions that disagree completely and all have a case.

activities.title: Drive Highway 1 down the Big Sur coast
activities.description: Cliffs, bridges and fog between Monterey and San Simeon. Landslides close sections regularly — check before committing.

activities.title: Watch autumn colour move through New England
activities.description: Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine turn from late September, tracked by foliage maps updated weekly.

activities.title: Ride the Alaska Railroad
activities.description: Anchorage to Denali and Fairbanks, past glaciers and moose, with open-air viewing cars in summer.

activities.title: See the Northern Lights from Alaska
activities.description: Fairbanks sits under the auroral oval, with dark, clear winter nights and hot springs to wait in.

activities.title: Snorkel or hike a Hawaiian island
activities.description: Volcanic craters, waterfalls and reefs — Kauai for greenery, Big Island for lava, Maui for the road to Hana.

activities.title: Paddle the Everglades
activities.description: A river of grass moving inches an hour, with alligators, manatees and 350 bird species. Mosquitoes rule the wet season.

activities.title: Stand at the mist of Niagara Falls
activities.description: The Canadian side has the better view, but the American side puts you closer to the base on the Cave of the Winds decks.

activities.title: Walk the National Mall museums
activities.description: The Smithsonian's museums are free — air and space, natural history, and the African American History museum that books out weeks ahead.

activities.title: Drive Route 66 in pieces
activities.description: The original road is broken up now, but long stretches survive through Arizona and New Mexico with the neon still lit.

activities.title: Sleep out under a dark sky
activities.description: Big Bend, Great Basin and much of Utah are certified dark-sky areas, with the Milky Way visible to the naked eye.

activities.title: Take a college-town Saturday at face value
activities.description: Tailgates, marching bands and 100,000 people in one stadium — the closest thing the country has to a shared ritual.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.blurb: A young island still being built — lava fields, glaciers grinding to the sea, and geothermal water coming out of the ground hot enough to cook in.
countries.uniqueness: Iceland sits on the split between two tectonic plates, which is why the landscape looks unfinished: new lava, active volcanoes, and enough geothermal heat that most homes and pools are warmed straight from the ground. The daylight swings from near-endless in June to four hours in December, which changes what's possible more than the temperature does.

seasons.label: Midnight sun
seasons.note: Barely gets dark, highland roads open, puffins nesting, and every trail accessible. The busiest and priciest window — and no northern lights, because there's no night.

seasons.label: Aurora shoulder
seasons.note: September is one of the two strongest months for northern lights, with roads still easy and autumn colour on the moss. Nights are dark enough again.

seasons.label: Deep winter
seasons.note: Four or five hours of low golden light, ice caves at their most stable, and lights on clear nights. Some roads close without notice.

seasons.label: Late winter
seasons.note: Widely rated the best aurora window — stable weather, long dark nights, and heightened activity near the March equinox. Solar activity remains elevated through 2026 after the recent cycle peak.

activities.title: Wait out a clear night for the aurora
activities.description: It needs darkness, clear sky and solar activity all at once. Away from Reykjavík's glow is enough — you don't need to go far, just out.

activities.title: Drive the Golden Circle
activities.description: Þingvellir's rift valley where the plates pull apart, the Geysir field, and Gullfoss dropping into a canyon. All within a day of the capital.

activities.title: Walk behind Seljalandsfoss
activities.description: A waterfall with a path running behind the curtain of water. You will get wet, and in winter the path ices over and closes.

activities.title: Stand on the black sand at Reynisfjara
activities.description: Basalt columns, sea stacks and Atlantic surf. The waves here are genuinely dangerous — people have been swept off this beach.

activities.title: Watch icebergs drift at Jökulsárlón
activities.description: A glacial lagoon calving into the sea, with the ice washing back up on the black beach opposite — locally called Diamond Beach.

activities.title: Go inside a glacier ice cave
activities.description: Blue chambers under the ice, only stable and safe in the cold months, and only with a guide. They melt and reform each year.

activities.title: Snorkel between two continents at Silfra
activities.description: A fissure in Þingvellir filled with glacial meltwater filtered through lava for decades — visibility runs to about 100 metres. Drysuit, year-round, 2°C.

activities.title: Soak in geothermal water
activities.description: The Blue Lagoon is the famous one; Sky Lagoon, Mývatn Nature Baths and the local swimming pool in every town do the same job for less.

activities.title: Drive the full Ring Road
activities.description: 1,332km around the island. Ten days does it comfortably; a week is a rush. The east and north see a fraction of the south coast's traffic.

activities.title: Get into the highlands
activities.description: Landmannalaugar's rhyolite hills and Þórsmörk's valleys, reached on gravel F-roads that only open once the snow clears.

activities.title: Hike the Laugavegur trail
activities.description: Fifty-odd kilometres over four days through hot springs, black desert and glacial rivers you wade across, staying in mountain huts.

activities.title: Watch puffins on the cliffs
activities.description: Millions nest around the coast each summer — the Westman Islands, Látrabjarg and Dyrhólaey are the reliable spots.

activities.title: Go whale watching from Húsavík
activities.description: A small northern harbour that calls itself Europe's whale capital — humpbacks and minke through summer, blue whales occasionally.

activities.title: Take the ferry to the Westfjords
activities.description: The remotest corner of the country: Dynjandi's tiered waterfall, Arctic foxes, cliffs full of birds and almost no other cars.

activities.title: Walk on a glacier with crampons
activities.description: Sólheimajökull and Vatnajökull outlets are the accessible ones. Never without a guide — crevasses open and shift constantly.

activities.title: See where a volcano recently erupted
activities.description: The Reykjanes peninsula has erupted repeatedly in recent years, leaving fresh lava fields near the capital. Access depends entirely on current conditions.

activities.title: Try the food people warn you about
activities.description: Fermented shark and sheep's head exist mainly for tourists now. The lamb soup, skyr, rye bread baked in the ground and hot dogs are the real staples.

activities.title: Eat at a harbour fish shack
activities.description: Cod and langoustine straight off the boats — Reykjavík's old harbour, Höfn for lobster, and small places all round the coast.

activities.title: Spend a night in Reykjavík
activities.description: The world's northernmost capital is small enough to cross on foot — Hallgrímskirkja's tower, Harpa's glass facade, and bars that don't fill until midnight.

activities.title: Ride an Icelandic horse
activities.description: A breed kept pure for a thousand years, with a fifth gait — the tölt — smooth enough to drink coffee at speed.

activities.title: Sit in a pool at midnight in June
activities.description: The sun never properly sets, so the town pool at 1am is still light and still open. Locals treat it as normal.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.blurb: Medinas that swallow your sense of direction, mountains with snow above palm valleys, and the Sahara close enough to reach in an afternoon.
countries.uniqueness: Few countries compress this much geography: Atlantic surf, a 4,000-metre mountain range, and true desert dunes all within a day's drive. The medinas of Fez and Marrakech are among the largest car-free urban areas on earth — they predate the wheel as a design constraint.

seasons.label: Spring
seasons.note: The strongest window — comfortable in the cities, wildflowers in the Atlas, and the desert warm rather than punishing.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Inland regularly passes 40°C and the Sahara becomes genuinely hard going. The Atlantic coast around Essaouira stays cool and windy.

seasons.label: Autumn
seasons.note: The other sweet spot: heat easing, date harvest in the south, and clear skies for the mountains.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Cold nights in the desert and snow in the High Atlas. Marrakech stays mild by day; the north can be wet.

activities.title: Get lost in the Fez medina
activities.description: Roughly 9,000 lanes, no cars, and donkeys still carrying the freight. Getting lost isn't a risk here, it's the default state.

activities.title: Look down on the Chouara tanneries
activities.description: Stone dye pits worked by hand since medieval times, viewed from the leather shops' terraces. They hand you mint for the smell, and you'll need it.

activities.title: Watch Jemaa el-Fnaa fill up at dusk
activities.description: Marrakech's main square shifts through the day from snake charmers to food stalls to storytellers, and is busiest well after dark.

activities.title: Ride a camel into the Erg Chebbi dunes
activities.description: Sand up to 150 metres high near Merzouga, usually done as an overnight with a desert camp and no light pollution at all.

activities.title: Sleep out under the Sahara sky
activities.description: Camps range from basic to elaborate. The reason to go is the silence and the stars, neither of which appear in the brochure photos.

activities.title: Trek in the High Atlas from Imlil
activities.description: Berber villages, walnut terraces and mule tracks. Toubkal, North Africa's highest peak at 4,167m, is a two-day climb from here.

activities.title: Walk the Todra or Dades gorges
activities.description: Red rock walls narrowing to a few metres, with a river and a road running through and climbers on the faces above.

activities.title: Sip mint tea on a Chefchaouen rooftop
activities.description: The blue city in the Rif mountains — every wall repainted each year, and best appreciated slowly from above.

activities.title: See the kasbah at Aït Benhaddou
activities.description: A fortified mud-brick village on the old caravan route, rebuilt repeatedly for films and still standing above the river.

activities.title: Eat a tagine that cooked for hours
activities.description: The conical pot steams its own contents — lamb with prunes, chicken with preserved lemon and olives. Nothing like the fast versions abroad.

activities.title: Have a Friday couscous
activities.description: The traditional family meal after prayers, steamed three times over a broth. Ask a day ahead in most riads and they'll make it.

activities.title: Take a cooking class in a riad
activities.description: Usually starts in the souk buying spices, ends on a rooftop eating what you made. Riads are courtyard houses turned guesthouses.

activities.title: Eat grilled sardines on the Essaouira quay
activities.description: Boats unload in the morning and the grills start immediately. Windy, gull-heavy, and among the cheapest good meals in the country.

activities.title: Learn to windsurf or surf at Essaouira
activities.description: Reliable Atlantic wind has made this a kitesurfing town; Taghazout further south is the mellower surf option.

activities.title: Bathe in a hammam
activities.description: Steam, black soap, and being scrubbed harder than expected. Public ones are cheap and communal; riads offer the gentler version.

activities.title: Walk the Majorelle and Yves Saint Laurent gardens
activities.description: Cobalt-blue walls, cactus and bamboo in the middle of Marrakech, with the YSL museum next door.

activities.title: See the Hassan II mosque in Casablanca
activities.description: Built partly over the Atlantic, with a minaret 210 metres tall. One of the few mosques in Morocco open to non-Muslim visitors.

activities.title: Wander the Roman ruins at Volubilis
activities.description: Mosaic floors and standing columns on a hillside near Meknes, at the far southwestern edge of what Rome controlled.

activities.title: Bargain properly in the souks
activities.description: Expected, and treated as conversation rather than conflict. Walking away is part of it, and so is the tea.

activities.title: Take the train between the imperial cities
activities.description: Fast, cheap and comfortable between Tangier, Rabat, Casablanca, Meknes and Fez — far easier than driving.

activities.title: Stay in a riad courtyard
activities.description: Blank walls onto the lane, then a fountain, orange trees and open sky inside. The whole point of the architecture is the contrast.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.blurb: Five thousand years of building, most of it within sight of one river, and a desert that starts the moment the irrigation stops.
countries.uniqueness: Almost the entire population lives on about 4% of the land — the thin green strip along the Nile. Fly over it and the country reads as a river with edges. That concentration is why the monuments sit so close together, and why a boat is still the natural way to see them.

seasons.label: Peak season
seasons.note: The comfortable window, and the right time for a Nile cruise. Warm days, cool nights, and desert mornings that need a jacket.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.note: Coolest and busiest, especially around Christmas and New Year. Upper Egypt stays pleasant while Cairo can be genuinely chilly at night.

seasons.label: Shoulder
seasons.note: Warm without being punishing, and slightly quieter at the big sites. Spring can bring khamsin dust winds.

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.note: Luxor and Aswan regularly pass 40°C — sightseeing means starting at dawn and stopping by eleven. Red Sea diving stays good, and prices drop hard.

activities.title: Watch sunrise over the Giza pyramids
activities.description: Arriving at opening puts you on the plateau before the buses. The Sphinx and three pyramids sit on the edge of the city, not in empty desert.

activities.title: Go inside the Great Pyramid
activities.description: A cramped, hot climb up the Grand Gallery to a bare granite chamber. Claustrophobic, and worth it for the engineering alone.

activities.title: See Tutankhamun's treasures at the Grand Egyptian Museum
activities.description: The new museum beside the pyramids holds the full Tutankhamun collection together for the first time, plus Khufu's solar boat.

activities.title: Walk into the tombs of the Valley of the Kings
activities.description: Painted burial chambers cut deep into rock near Luxor, colours still vivid. Tickets cover three tombs; Seti I and Nefertari cost extra.

activities.title: Stand in the hypostyle hall at Karnak
activities.description: 134 columns, some 21 metres tall, in a temple complex built and rebuilt over roughly 2,000 years.

activities.title: See Luxor Temple lit after dark
activities.description: Open into the evening, far cooler, and floodlighting that makes the reliefs read better than daylight does.

activities.title: Cruise the Nile between Luxor and Aswan
activities.description: Three or four days on the water, stopping at Edfu and Kom Ombo, watching farmland and mudbrick villages slide past.

activities.title: Sail a felucca at sunset
activities.description: Traditional lateen-rigged boats with no engine — just wind, current and a boatman. Aswan's stretch of river is the classic one.

activities.title: See Abu Simbel
activities.description: Two temples cut into a cliff by Ramesses II, sawn into blocks and moved uphill in the 1960s to escape the rising lake behind the dam.

activities.title: Dive or snorkel the Red Sea
activities.description: Coral in extremely clear, warm water off Dahab, Hurghada and Marsa Alam. Dahab's Blue Hole is famous and has killed a number of divers.

activities.title: Swim with dugongs or dolphins at Marsa Alam
activities.description: Seagrass beds south of Hurghada support dugongs, and offshore reefs have resident spinner dolphins.

activities.title: Climb Mount Sinai for sunrise
activities.description: A three-hour night walk up steps and camel path to a summit with a chapel, timed to arrive before first light.

activities.title: Drive into the White Desert
activities.description: Chalk formations eroded into mushrooms and towers, camped in overnight from Bahariya oasis. Absolute silence.

activities.title: Wander Islamic Cairo
activities.description: Medieval mosques, madrasas and gates around Al-Muizz street, plus the Khan el-Khalili bazaar and its 14th-century courtyards.

activities.title: Sit in a Cairo ahwa
activities.description: Old coffeehouses with backgammon, shisha and mint tea. El Fishawy in Khan el-Khalili has reputedly been open continuously for two centuries.

activities.title: Eat koshari from a street counter
activities.description: Rice, lentils, macaroni, chickpeas, fried onion and tomato sauce in one bowl. The national dish, and usually about a dollar.

activities.title: Try ful and ta'ameya for breakfast
activities.description: Slow-cooked fava beans and Egyptian falafel made from the same bean, eaten from carts from early morning.

activities.title: See Coptic Cairo
activities.description: The Hanging Church, Ben Ezra synagogue and the Coptic Museum in a small walled quarter — a reminder Egypt isn't only pharaonic and Islamic.

activities.title: Visit Siwa Oasis
activities.description: Near the Libyan border, with salt lakes you float in, a mudbrick fortress town, and its own Berber language and customs.

activities.title: Walk Alexandria's corniche
activities.description: A Mediterranean city with Greek and Roman layers underneath, the Bibliotheca Alexandrina above ground, and seafood along the seafront.

activities.title: Ride the sleeper train to Aswan
activities.description: Overnight from Cairo in a cabin, waking up alongside the Nile. Slower than flying, and a completely different view of the country.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.blurb: A thousand miles of coast, limestone rising out of rice fields, and a food culture that changes completely between one city and the next.
countries.uniqueness: Vietnam is long and thin enough to have three separate climates running on different schedules — the north has a genuine cool season while the south stays warm year-round. It means there's almost always somewhere in the country at its best, and almost never a month that suits all of it.

seasons.label: North — cool and dry
seasons.note: Hanoi, Halong Bay and Sapa at their clearest. December and January can be genuinely cold, with mist over the bay.

seasons.label: North — hot and wet
seasons.note: Humid with heavy afternoon rain, but the rice terraces at Sapa are green through summer and gold around September.

seasons.label: Central
seasons.note: The window for Hoi An, Hue and Da Nang. The northeast monsoon brings heavy rain here from October to December, with flooding common.

seasons.label: South
seasons.note: Ho Chi Minh City and the Mekong Delta at their driest. The southwest monsoon brings rain April to October, usually in short bursts.

activities.title: Sleep overnight on Halong Bay
activities.description: Nearly 2,000 limestone islands in a shallow bay. Day trips see the crowded part; overnight boats reach quieter water like Lan Ha and Bai Tu Long.

activities.title: Kayak between the karsts
activities.description: Paddling under low arches into hidden lagoons is the part of Halong the big boats can't do.

activities.title: Take a boat through Tam Coc or Trang An
activities.description: Called the inland Halong — the same limestone towers rising out of flooded rice paddies, rowed through caves by women using their feet.

activities.title: Trek between hill villages around Sapa
activities.description: Terraced rice fields cut into mountains near the Chinese border, home to Hmong and Dao communities. Homestays are common.

activities.title: Ride the Hai Van Pass
activities.description: A coastal mountain road between Hue and Da Nang, with the sea on one side and cloud usually sitting on the summit.

activities.title: Go into the caves at Phong Nha
activities.description: Some of the largest caves on earth, including Son Doong, which has its own weather. Cheaper caves like Paradise and Hang En are open to anyone.

activities.title: Have clothes made in Hoi An
activities.description: A lantern-lit old trading port with hundreds of tailors. Two fittings over a couple of days is the usual rhythm.

activities.title: See Hoi An lit by lanterns
activities.description: The old town goes lantern-only on the full moon each month, with candles floated on the river.

activities.title: Walk the citadel and tombs at Hue
activities.description: The imperial capital until 1945 — a walled palace complex damaged in the war, and emperors' tombs spread along the Perfume River.

activities.title: Eat pho for breakfast where it belongs
activities.description: Northern pho is clear and plain; the southern version arrives with herbs and sauces. Both are breakfast food, not dinner.

activities.title: Work through a banh mi
activities.description: French bread, Vietnamese fillings — a colonial hangover that turned into one of the world's best sandwiches. Hoi An's are famous for good reason.

activities.title: Drink egg coffee in Hanoi
activities.description: Whipped yolk and condensed milk over strong coffee, invented during a milk shortage in the 1940s and never abandoned.

activities.title: Eat on plastic stools in the Old Quarter
activities.description: Hanoi's 36 streets, each historically for one trade, with bun cha and beer hoi served at knee height on the pavement.

activities.title: Take a boat through the Mekong Delta
activities.description: Floating markets at Cai Rang trading from boat to boat at dawn, coconut candy workshops and channels barely wider than the sampan.

activities.title: Go into the Cu Chi tunnels
activities.description: Kilometres of hand-dug wartime tunnels outside Ho Chi Minh City, some widened enough for visitors to crawl through.

activities.title: See the War Remnants Museum
activities.description: A blunt, difficult account of the American War from the Vietnamese side. Not an easy visit, and the most important one in Saigon.

activities.title: Cross the road in Ho Chi Minh City
activities.description: Thousands of scooters and no gaps. The technique is to walk slowly and predictably and let the traffic flow around you.

activities.title: Ride the Reunification Express
activities.description: Hanoi to Saigon over roughly 33 hours, hugging the coast. Most people take it in sections rather than end to end.

activities.title: Motorbike the Ha Giang loop
activities.description: Three or four days of mountain switchbacks near the Chinese border, through the country's most dramatic karst landscape. Easy riders take you as passenger.

activities.title: Swim off Phu Quoc or Con Dao
activities.description: Islands off the south coast — Phu Quoc developed and easy, Con Dao remote, with a hard prison history and empty beaches.

activities.title: Sit with a Vietnamese drip coffee
activities.description: The metal filter takes several minutes to drip through, which is the point. Robusta, strong, usually over condensed milk and ice.

countries.name: Peru
countries.blurb: Three countries stacked into one — desert coast, high Andes, and Amazon rainforest — with a food scene that has quietly become one of the world's best.
countries.uniqueness: Peru holds a coastal desert, 6,000-metre peaks and a share of the Amazon within a few hours' flight of each other, which is why the ingredient list is so long. It's also where the potato was domesticated — several thousand varieties still grow in the Andes, most of which never leave the country.

seasons.label: Dry season (highlands)
seasons.note: The main window for Cusco, Machu Picchu and trekking — clear days, cold nights, and the busiest months. Book permits and trains well ahead.

seasons.label: Shoulder
seasons.note: Green landscape, fewer people, and a reasonable chance of dry days. Often the best balance of the year.

seasons.label: Wet season
seasons.note: Afternoon rain, muddy trails and cloud over the peaks, but lush scenery and far fewer visitors. The Inca Trail closes entirely each February for maintenance — in 2026, 1–28 February — though Machu Picchu itself stays open.

seasons.label: Coast and Amazon
seasons.note: Lima is grey and misty May–November and sunny December–April — the opposite of the mountains. The Amazon is hot and humid throughout, wettest December–April.

activities.title: Reach Machu Picchu early
activities.description: An Inca citadel on a ridge above the Urubamba, cloud usually burning off mid-morning. Entry is by timed slot and route, decided when you book.

activities.title: Trek the classic Inca Trail
activities.description: Four days over two high passes on original Inca paving, arriving through the Sun Gate at dawn. Permits are capped and sell out months ahead.

activities.title: Take the Salkantay or Lares route instead
activities.description: Alternative treks to the same destination — Salkantay is higher and wilder, Lares passes through weaving villages. No permit cap.

activities.title: Climb to Rainbow Mountain
activities.description: Mineral-striped slopes above 5,000m, a hard day out on thin air. Acclimatise in Cusco for several days first.

activities.title: Walk the salt pans at Maras
activities.description: Thousands of terraced evaporation ponds fed by a salt spring, worked by local families since Inca times.

activities.title: See the circular terraces at Moray
activities.description: Concentric agricultural terraces with a measurable temperature difference between top and bottom — widely read as a crop laboratory.

activities.title: Look at the stonework at Sacsayhuamán
activities.description: Blocks weighing hundreds of tonnes fitted without mortar so tightly a blade won't go between them, on the hill above Cusco.

activities.title: Spend time in Cusco itself
activities.description: Inca foundations with colonial buildings on top, at 3,400m. Worth two or three days purely to acclimatise before anything strenuous.

activities.title: Fly over the Nazca Lines
activities.description: Enormous figures scratched into the desert floor two thousand years ago, only legible from the air. Small planes, short flights, bumpy.

activities.title: Float across Lake Titicaca to the Uros islands
activities.description: Reed islands built and rebuilt by hand on the world's highest navigable lake. Taquile and Amantaní offer homestays further out.

activities.title: Go into the Amazon from Puerto Maldonado or Iquitos
activities.description: Lodges on the river with night walks, canopy towers and oxbow lakes. Iquitos is reachable only by boat or plane.

activities.title: Watch condors at Colca Canyon
activities.description: Twice the depth of the Grand Canyon, with Andean condors riding the morning thermals up the walls.

activities.title: Take a boat to the Ballestas Islands
activities.description: Sea lions, Humboldt penguins and dense seabird colonies off the Paracas coast — often called the poor man's Galápagos.

activities.title: Eat ceviche at a Lima market counter
activities.description: Raw fish cured in lime with chilli and onion, eaten at lunch when the catch is fresh — never at dinner, if you ask a Peruvian.

activities.title: Eat at one of Lima's tasting-menu restaurants
activities.description: Central, Maido and Kjolle regularly appear near the top of the world's restaurant lists, built around Peruvian ecosystems and ingredients.

activities.title: Try a pisco sour where it's argued over
activities.description: Grape brandy, lime, egg white and bitters — with Chile contesting the origin, which Peruvians will happily explain at length.

activities.title: Wander a highland market day
activities.description: Pisac and Chinchero fill with produce, textiles and trade. Sunday is the big day, and the mornings are for locals rather than tour buses.

activities.title: Sandboard the dunes at Huacachina
activities.description: A palm-ringed desert oasis surrounded by dunes tall enough to make your stomach drop, ridden down on boards or in dune buggies.

activities.title: Surf the long left at Chicama
activities.description: Reputedly the longest left-hand wave in the world, on the north coast — rides measured in minutes rather than seconds.

activities.title: Ride the train through the Sacred Valley
activities.description: The line to Aguas Calientes follows the river through a gorge that road traffic can't reach. Panoramic carriages, and worth the window seat.

activities.title: See how alpaca textiles are actually made
activities.description: Weaving cooperatives around Chinchero demonstrate natural dyeing and backstrap looms — and explain why the cheap 'alpaca' in markets isn't.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.blurb: Pyramids in jungle, colonial cities in silver country, two coastlines, and food with UNESCO heritage status that mostly gets eaten standing up.
countries.uniqueness: Mexico has more UNESCO World Heritage sites than any country in the Americas, and its cuisine was the first ever listed as intangible heritage in its own right. Underneath the Yucatán there's no surface river at all — rainwater drains through limestone into thousands of flooded caves, which is why cenotes exist and why the Maya built their cities around them.

seasons.label: Dry season
seasons.note: The main window nationwide — warm, dry and reliably sunny. December to March is peak on both coasts, with prices to match.

seasons.label: Shoulder
seasons.note: Hot but quieter, before or after the rains. Good value, and the Yucatán is at its emptiest.

seasons.label: Rainy season
seasons.note: Afternoon downpours rather than all-day rain, landscapes at their greenest, and hurricane risk on both coasts peaking August–September.

seasons.label: Highlands
seasons.note: Mexico City and San Miguel sit high enough to stay temperate all year — warm days, cool evenings, and rain concentrated in summer afternoons.

activities.title: Climb the pyramids at Teotihuacán
activities.description: A city of 100,000 people abandoned centuries before the Aztecs found it, with the Avenue of the Dead running between two enormous pyramids.

activities.title: See Chichén Itzá at the equinox — or avoid it then
activities.description: The main pyramid throws a serpent-shaped shadow down its staircase at the March and September equinoxes, which draws enormous crowds.

activities.title: Walk into the jungle ruins at Palenque or Calakmul
activities.description: Maya cities still half-swallowed by rainforest, with howler monkeys in the canopy. Calakmul is remote enough to be nearly empty.

activities.title: Spend a day at the Anthropology Museum
activities.description: Mexico City's national museum holds the Aztec sun stone and Maya collections — widely considered one of the best museums anywhere.

activities.title: Swim in a cenote
activities.description: Limestone sinkholes filled with fresh water, some open to the sky, others in caves with light shafts. The Yucatán has thousands.

activities.title: Snorkel the Mesoamerican Reef
activities.description: The second-largest barrier reef in the world, running down the coast from Cancún past Cozumel toward Belize.

activities.title: Swim with whale sharks off Isla Holbox
activities.description: The largest fish in the sea gathers off the north Yucatán coast to feed in summer. Regulated, with limits on boats and swimmers.

activities.title: Watch grey whales in Baja
activities.description: They migrate to Baja's lagoons to calve, and mothers regularly bring calves right up to the small boats.

activities.title: Stand in the monarch butterfly forests
activities.description: Hundreds of millions of butterflies overwinter in the Michoacán highlands, weighing down the fir branches until the sun warms them.

activities.title: Eat tacos al pastor from a spit
activities.description: Pork on a vertical trompo — a Lebanese immigrant technique adopted entirely — sliced with pineapple, eaten late at night.

activities.title: Try the seven moles of Oaxaca
activities.description: Sauces with dozens of ingredients ground for hours. Negro is the famous one, but coloradito and amarillo are worth the comparison.

activities.title: Drink mezcal in a palenque
activities.description: Small distilleries around Oaxaca roast agave in earth pits, which is where the smoke comes from. Tasted neat, with orange and salt.

activities.title: Eat breakfast in a city market
activities.description: Mercado 20 de Noviembre in Oaxaca, San Juan in Mexico City — tlayudas, tamales, fresh juice, and the best value meal of the day.

activities.title: Be there for Día de Muertos
activities.description: Cemetery vigils, marigolds and altars for the dead — a family occasion rather than a party, at its most striking around Oaxaca and Michoacán.

activities.title: Take a boat through the canals at Xochimilco
activities.description: The last surviving stretch of the Aztec lake system, punted on painted trajineras with mariachi boats pulling alongside.

activities.title: Wander the colonial cities of the highlands
activities.description: San Miguel de Allende, Guanajuato and Puebla — silver money spent on churches and pastel streets, still very much lived in.

activities.title: See Frida Kahlo's blue house
activities.description: Casa Azul in Coyoacán, where she was born, lived and died, with her studio and belongings left in place. Tickets go quickly.

activities.title: Ride the Copper Canyon railway
activities.description: A line through canyon country in Chihuahua that's deeper and longer than the Grand Canyon, past Rarámuri villages.

activities.title: Surf the Pacific coast
activities.description: Puerto Escondido's Zicatela is for experts; Sayulita, Troncones and San Pancho are where people actually learn.

activities.title: Walk the beaches at Tulum or Holbox
activities.description: Ruins on a cliff above the Caribbean at Tulum; sandbars, flamingos and no cars on Holbox further north.

activities.title: Watch lucha libre from the cheap seats
activities.description: Masked wrestling in Mexico City's Arena México, taken seriously and not seriously at the same time. The crowd is the show.
